summary: A steel light tower on a concrete pier in Green Bay, built in the 1930s to replace the Eleven Foot Shoal lightship; manned until about 1979, now automated and not open to visitors.

notes_for_editor: Thin primary evidence: no NRHP text (not digitised), no Lighthouse Board/Bulletin page beyond one 1936 passage. Much rests on Lighthouse Friends (facts only) and a July 2026 Daily Press feature. First-lit date (1935 vs 1936) and automation (1979 vs 1980) unresolved. Outcome of the 2017 auction not found; LHF still lists Coast Guard as owner. Fog signal: LHF 1936 text says diaphone, Daily Press says electric. Pier height: LHF 21 ft above water, Daily Press 12 ft. Kenneth L. Crowe roster line merges two USCG entries. Location says Michigan though the 1936 Bulletin index prints 'Wis.'. Outcome of the 2017 auction not reported in the sources cited. Distance from Peninsula Point: Daily Press 'nearly seven miles', USLHS '10 miles', LHF '9.6 miles'. Bulletin 1936 passage: issue month not determined (PDF page 30 of the 1936 volume). Crew storm quote in the Daily Press is undated (between 1955 and 1979).
